- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In low-sentiment (negative or neutral) environments, model often underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next period.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day mean in high-sentiment periods; adjust mean forecast downward by 1–2% if sentiment > 0.10.
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., ±0.15 or more), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±1–2% deviation from trend for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment turns.
- Model underestimates price drops in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next period if sentiment < -0.10.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, flag for correction — reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to overreact to short-term spikes — apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 1–2% per spike.
